standard.title: Organise activities with peers
standard.description: engage in modelled non-verbal, spoken and written exchanges with peers to organise activities relating to daily life and school environment
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interact using modelled language for personal exchange and classroom routines (AC9LS8EC01, AC9LS8EC02). They have not yet used the target language to organise joint activities or communicate across non-verbal, spoken and written modes simultaneously.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students engage in non-verbal, spoken and written exchanges in the target language with peers to plan, organise and carry out activities related to daily life and the school environment, using modelled language appropriate to context.

nodes.label: Coordinating and planning with peers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use modelled spoken and written exchanges to coordinate a simple joint activity with a peer in the target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in one structured planning or organising exchange with a peer (e.g. assigning roles, agreeing on a plan) using at least three modelled phrases.
nodes.typical_width: Use spoken and written modelled language to plan, negotiate and carry out a collaborative activity; exchange messages or notes about plans, timings or roles using present and near-future structures.
wider: Use a secure digital messaging or email platform to plan a real or simulated activity with a peer entirely in the target language
Compare how organising language differs between spoken and written modes in the target language — identify conventions specific to each

response_modes.reason: Students need exposure to a range of organising exchanges (assigning, scheduling, confirming, adjusting) before they can manage the planning demands of EC03's collaborative tasks. Building this repertoire through varied simulated planning scenarios is the primary lever.

success_criteria: Can produce at least three modelled phrases to coordinate a joint activity with a peer in the target language
Can exchange a short written message (note or digital message) in the target language about a planned activity

nodes.label: Non-verbal communication and multimodal exchanges
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise the role of non-verbal communication in the target language context and combine non-verbal, spoken and written elements in exchanges.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in one exchange that requires combining at least two modes (e.g. spoken + gesture, written + visual) in the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Engage in modelled scenarios (e.g. simulated transactions, directions, collaborative tasks) that require coordinating spoken, written and non-verbal elements; recognise culturally specific non-verbal conventions in the target language community.
wider: Participate in a charades or mime scenario and reflect on which meanings transfer across cultures and which require cultural knowledge to interpret
Produce a bilingual resource (poster, flyer, digital notice) that combines visual and written elements to communicate to a mixed-language audience

response_modes.reason: Non-verbal conventions in the target language vary significantly across cultural communities. Exposure to varied scenarios prevents students from assuming that non-verbal cues are universal — a misconception with practical intercultural consequences.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Non-verbal and multimodal communication is a concrete, accessible entry point into intercultural understanding at Y7-8. Recognising that gesture and convention are culturally variable rather than universal builds the metalinguistic awareness that deepens across the sequence.
success_criteria: Can combine at least two communication modes (spoken, written, non-verbal) in a single organised exchange
Can identify at least one non-verbal convention in the target language community that differs from Australian English norms

nodes.label: Simulated and real transactions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can participate in simulated or real transactional exchanges (e.g. purchasing, requesting services, following directions) in the target language.
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in one scripted or semi-scripted transactional role-play in the target language (e.g. a simulated purchase, asking for and giving directions).
nodes.typical_width: Engage in a range of simulated transactional scenarios; use modelled language for requesting, responding, clarifying and completing a transaction; integrate asking strategies from EC02.
wider: Navigate a real or simulated digital service (e.g. a map, timetable or menu from a target language community) to locate and act on information
Produce a class resource (signs, posters, reference materials) in the target language that could support real transactions in a target language environment

response_modes.reason: Transactional exchanges require students to simultaneously manage topic vocabulary, asking strategies (EC02), appropriate register (EC01) and non-verbal conventions (node 2). Role-play scenarios that require all of these to operate together are the key teaching structure.

success_criteria: Can complete a basic transactional exchange (request, respond, clarify) in a modelled scenario using target language
Integrates at least one asking or clarifying strategy from prior learning into the exchange
